lfs.fetchAllHint: Gets every version of every LFS file from the server — needs a lot of space; rarely needed.
lfs.pruneHint: Deletes old local copies of LFS files that are already on the server and not used by the current checkout. They can be downloaded again later.

lfs.pruneWould_other: {{count}} objects can be deleted, freeing {{size}} ({{kept}} kept)

lfs.pruneWouldApprox_other: About {{count}} objects can be deleted, up to {{size}} ({{kept}} kept)

lfs.pruneConfirmBody_one: {{count}} object ({{size}}) will be deleted from this computer. It stays on the server.
lfs.pruneConfirmBody_other: {{count}} objects ({{size}}) will be deleted from this computer. They stay on the server.
lfs.fsckHint: Checks that LFS objects are intact and that files matching LFS patterns were committed as pointers.

fsckKind.missing_other: {{count}} objects are not on this computer

fsckHelp.missing: Not downloaded yet (or deleted): download them from the Files tab.
fsckHelp.corrupt: The local copy is damaged: delete it from .git/lfs/objects and download it again.
fsckHelp.nonCanonicalPointer: A pointer file was edited by hand; re-add the file so LFS rewrites it.
fsckHelp.notAPointer: These files match an LFS pattern but were committed as normal git files (often before the pattern existed). For unpushed commits use the check below; otherwise ask your team before rewriting history.

ssh.title: SSH keys — {{account}}
ssh.description: SSH keys are used for repositories bound to this account with the SSH transport. The app injects the default key through GIT_SSH_COMMAND, so no host alias is needed in ~/.ssh/config and remotes keep the plain git@host:org/repo.git form.
ssh.empty: This account has no SSH key yet. Generate a new key or import an existing one.

generateForm.title: Generate an Ed25519 key
generateForm.commentHint: Leave empty to use the default identity's email.
generateForm.passphraseHint: The passphrase is saved in the OS keychain so git can use the key without prompting.

importForm.title: Import a private key
importForm.passphraseRequired: This key is protected by a passphrase — enter it and try again.
importForm.alreadyKnown: This key is already in the account.
importForm.alreadyOther: This key is attached to another account.
importForm.publicMismatch: The .pub file next to the key does not match the private key — the public key from the private key was used.
importForm.note: Your file is not modified: the app stores a copy in its data folder, readable by the current user only.

uploadResult.uploaded: Public key uploaded to the provider.
uploadResult.alreadyRegistered: The key is already on this account — marked as uploaded.
uploadResult.usedByAnotherAccount: The provider says this key is registered to another account. A key can belong to one user only — generate a new key for this account.
uploadResult.missingScope: The token cannot add SSH keys (needs {{scopes}}). Sign in again granting it, or copy the public key and paste it in the provider's SSH settings.
uploadResult.missingScopeUnknown: The provider refused to add the key: the token lacks permission. Sign in again with SSH key management access, or paste the public key on the provider manually.
uploadResult.tokenPermissionMissing: The fine-grained token lacks the "Git SSH keys" (write) permission. Update the token or paste the public key on the provider manually.
uploadResult.noToken: The account has no token — sign in again to upload the key.
uploadResult.unauthorized: The token expired or was revoked — sign in again.

testResult.hostKeyFailed: The host key of {{host}} could not be verified.

failureHelp.invalidName: Branch/tag names cannot contain spaces or the characters ~ ^ : ? * [ \, and cannot start with -. Pick another name, e.g. feature/login.
failureHelp.invalidInput: Check what you entered (commit id, tag message…) and try again.
failureHelp.notFound: The branch, tag, commit or repository no longer exists. Click Fetch to refresh from the server, or check the remote URL.
failureHelp.alreadyExists: A branch/tag with that name already exists. Choose another name, or delete the old one first if you are sure it is not needed.
failureHelp.currentBranch: You cannot delete/rename the checked-out branch. Switch to another branch (e.g. main) first.
failureHelp.notFullyMerged: The branch has commits that are not merged anywhere — deleting it loses them. If you are sure, choose force delete.
failureHelp.localChanges: Uncommitted changes would be overwritten. Safe options: Commit them, or click Stash to put them aside and Pop them back later.
failureHelp.untrackedFiles: New (never committed) files have the same names as files about to be created. Commit them, stash them (tick 'include new files') or move them elsewhere.
failureHelp.unmergedFiles: Some files are still in conflict. Open each one under Conflicts, choose what to keep, mark it resolved, then click Continue.
failureHelp.operationInProgress: A merge/rebase/cherry-pick is in progress. Use the banner above to Continue (after resolving conflicts) or Abort to go back.
failureHelp.noOperation: Nothing is in progress — no action needed.
failureHelp.nothingToCommit: Nothing is staged. Stage files under 'Unstaged' first, or the change is already in the history.
failureHelp.nonFastForward: The server has commits you do not have yet. Click Pull to get them (resolve conflicts if any), then Push again. Avoid force push unless you are sure.
failureHelp.staleLease: Someone pushed to this branch after your last Fetch, so force push was stopped to avoid deleting their commits. Fetch, review the history, then decide.
failureHelp.remoteRejected: The server refused the change (usually a hook or a repository rule). Open 'Technical details' below to see the reason the server gave.
failureHelp.authFailed: The sign-in of {{account}} is no longer valid (token expired or revoked). Sign in again to get a new token.
failureHelp.connectionFailed: Could not reach the server. Check your network/VPN/proxy and the remote URL, then try again.
failureHelp.noUpstream: This branch is not linked to a branch on the server yet. Click Push — the app creates the remote branch and sets the upstream.
failureHelp.detachedHead: You are on a single commit, not on a branch (detached HEAD). Create a branch here or check out an existing branch first.
failureHelp.permissionDenied: {{account}} is signed in but cannot write to this repository. Switch to an account that can (account pill at the top), or ask the owner to add you as a collaborator.
failureHelp.workflowScope: You are pushing files under .github/workflows/ (GitHub Actions). GitHub requires the 'workflow' permission for that, and the current token of {{account}} does not have it. Click the button below to sign in again — GitHub asks you to grant the extra permission; click Authorize, then Push again. With a personal access token (PAT), create a new one with 'workflow' ticked.
failureHelp.protectedBranch: The repository owner protects this branch (no direct push, no force push or reviews required). Create a new branch, push it and open a Pull Request / Merge Request.
failureHelp.emailPrivacy: You enabled 'Block command line pushes that expose my email' on GitHub. Change the identity's email to your …@users.noreply.github.com address (see GitHub Settings → Emails), fix the author of the unpushed commits, then Push again.
failureHelp.secretDetected: An unpushed commit contains a password, API key or token. Remove it from the file, rewrite the commit (Amend, or reset before that commit and commit again), revoke/rotate the leaked secret, then Push again.

merge.explain: You are merging {{name}} into {{branch}}. “Mine” (git calls it ours) is the content on your current branch {{branch}}; “theirs” is the content from {{name}}.

mergeSquash.theirs: Theirs — the changes being squashed in
mergeSquash.explain: You are squashing (merge --squash) another branch's changes into {{branch}}. “Mine” (ours) is the current {{branch}}; “theirs” is the incoming changes.

rebase.explain: Careful during a rebase: git SWAPS the sides compared to a merge. “ours” is {{onto}} — the branch you are rebasing onto (plus the commits already replayed); “theirs” is your own commit {{commit}} from {{mine}}. To keep your code, pick “your commit”.

cherryPick.explain: You are cherry-picking commit {{commit}} onto {{branch}}. “Mine” (ours) is the current {{branch}}; “theirs” is the change brought by commit {{commit}}.

revert.explain: You are reverting (undoing) commit {{commit}}. “Ours” is the current code on {{branch}}; “theirs” is the code with the changes of {{commit}} taken out.

stash.explain: You are bringing back stashed changes. “Ours” is the current code on {{branch}}; “theirs” is what you stashed. On conflicts git keeps the stash — drop it once everything is resolved if you no longer need it.

applyMailbox.explain: You are applying a patch (git am) onto {{branch}}. “Ours” is the current code; “theirs” is the content of the patch.

unknown.explain: “Mine” (ours) is the version on {{branch}} (HEAD); “theirs” is the incoming version.
